version.changelog:
- Removed the file skill-card.md from the project. 
- No other changes were made to the skill's configuration or functionality.

llm.summary: The skill is a clearly disclosed Kia Access MCP setup guide with sensitive vehicle controls, but its risks are purpose-aligned and explicitly gated.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires Kia account credentials and can expose vehicle status and location, which is sensitive but proportionate to its stated vehicle-management purpose and disclosed in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses an MCP configuration entry that runs the external npm package via npx; this is a normal MCP installation pattern, but users must trust the referenced package because the artifact itself only contains setup instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly require explicit confirmation for commands, warn that dry runs do nothing, advise listing vehicles instead of guessing identifiers, and specifically caution against echoing passwords, refresh tokens, or session IDs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact discloses local remember-me token storage that can refresh sessions silently and provides a confirm-gated forget-session tool; it also warns that exported refresh tokens are plaintext MFA bypass credentials.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to let a user read and command their own Kia vehicle through Kia Access, and the documented tools match that purpose: vehicle status, location, EV charging, climate, lock, and unlock operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, verify that you trust the referenced npm package and source repository. Use KIA_WRITE_MODE=none or comfort unless door lock/unlock is truly needed, protect the Kia password and refresh token like account credentials, and require explicit confirmation before any vehicle command.
llm.findings: [AS2] expected: The scanner flagged MCP config access, but the artifact tells the user to add a server entry to .mcp.json or ~/.claude/mcp.json; it does not instruct the skill to read or harvest existing MCP configuration, tokens, or other integrations.
